examples.en: Our school starts the new semester on March 2.
The vacation ended and school started again today.

examples.ko: 내일 개학하면 친구들을 다시 만날 수 있어요.
examples.en: When school starts tomorrow, I can see my friends again.

examples.ko: 아이들이 개학할 때까지 가족 여행을 다녀올 거예요.
examples.en: We will go on a family trip before the kids go back to school.

examples.ko: 개학하는 날 아침에는 늘 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: On the morning school starts, I always feel heavy-hearted.
School has started, so the streets are crowded again.

explain: 방학이 끝나고 새 학기가 시작될 때 써요. 반대는 '방학하다'예요. 보통 '학교가 개학하다'처럼 학교를 주어로 써요. '입학하다'는 학교에 처음 들어갈 때 쓰니까 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when vacation ends and a new term starts. The opposite is '방학하다'. It is usually said with the school as the subject, like '학교가 개학하다'. '입학하다' is for entering a school for the first time, so it is different.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지가 큰 천둥소리에 겁먹고 침대 밑에 숨었어요.
examples.en: Our puppy got scared by the loud thunder and hid under the bed.
Don't be scared, it doesn't hurt at all.

examples.ko: 처음 비행기를 탔을 때 많이 겁먹었어요.
examples.en: I was really scared the first time I rode an airplane.

examples.ko: 뭘 그렇게 겁먹어요? 아무 일도 아니에요.
examples.en: What are you so scared of? It's nothing.
He looked at the teacher with a frightened face.

examples.ko: 겁먹을 필요 없어요. 면접은 금방 끝나요.
examples.en: There's no need to be scared. The interview ends quickly.

explain: '무서워하다'와 비슷하지만 '겁먹다'는 두려움이 마음에 들어와 움츠러든 모습을 말해요. '겁먹지 마'처럼 격려하는 말로 자주 나와요. '겁이 나다'는 두려운 마음이 저절로 생기는 느낌이고, '겁을 먹다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: It is similar to '무서워하다', but '겁먹다' shows someone shrinking back because fear has taken hold. It often appears in encouraging phrases like '겁먹지 마'. '겁이 나다' means fear arises on its own, and you can also split this word as '겁을 먹다'.

examples.en: The ball rolled slowly toward the goal.
The goalkeeper defended the goal until the end.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 골문 앞에서 기회를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: That player missed a chance right in front of the goal.
Before the match I checked whether the goal wobbled.

examples.ko: 상대 골문까지 달리는 데 오 초 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five seconds to run to the opponent's goal.
A net hangs on the goal.

explain: '골대'는 기둥과 가로대로 된 틀을 가리킬 때가 많고, '골문'은 공이 들어가는 입구 쪽을 가리켜요. 축구, 하키 같은 경기에서 써요.
explain_en: 골대 often points to the frame made of posts and a crossbar, while 골문 points to the opening the ball goes into. Both are used in sports like soccer and hockey.

examples.ko: 큰길 위에 새 영화 광고판이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: A billboard for a new movie was put up over the main road.

examples.ko: 버스 정류장 광고판을 보고 가수 이름을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned the singer's name from the ad board at the bus stop.

examples.ko: 광고판에는 신제품 사진이 크게 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The billboard shows a big picture of the new product.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 광고판의 불빛이 흐리게 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the light of the billboard looks blurry.
I decided to meet my friend in front of the billboard.
I heard the old billboard will be replaced with a new one tomorrow.

explain: '간판'은 가게가 자기 이름을 걸어 두는 판이고, 광고판은 광고를 보여 주는 판이에요. 불빛이 나오는 화면으로 된 것은 '전광판'이라고 해요. 길가나 건물 위에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: A '간판' is the sign a shop hangs with its own name, while 광고판 shows advertisements. One made of a lit-up screen is called a '전광판'. You can see them by the road or on top of buildings.

en: knowing glance; greeting with a nod

examples.en: I exchanged a nod with a neighbor in the elevator.

examples.ko: 말은 못 하고 눈인사만 짧게 나눴어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak, so we just briefly nodded at each other.

examples.ko: 선생님이 저를 보고 눈인사로 반겨 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher saw me and welcomed me with a nod.
It was during a meeting, so I just gave a light nod and walked past.

examples.ko: 매일 마주치니까 이제 눈인사 정도는 하는 사이예요.
examples.en: We run into each other every day, so we're at the nodding stage now.
I saw a friend greeting me with a nod from far away.

explain: 말을 하기 어려운 상황이거나 아주 친하지 않은 사이일 때 자주 해요. '눈인사를 하다/나누다/건네다'처럼 쓰고, '눈인사하다' 동사로도 말해요.
explain_en: People use it when speaking is awkward or when they are not very close. It goes with '눈인사를 하다/나누다/건네다', and '눈인사하다' also works as a verb.

examples.ko: 아침에 어머니가 미역국으로 생일상을 차려 주셨어요.
examples.en: In the morning, my mother set a birthday table with seaweed soup for me.

examples.ko: 혼자 먹는 생일상이 쓸쓸해서 친구에게 전화를 걸었어요.
examples.en: Eating a birthday meal alone felt lonely, so I called a friend.

examples.ko: 할머니 생일상에는 잡채와 떡이 꼭 올라가요.
examples.en: Japchae and rice cakes always go on Grandma's birthday table.

examples.ko: 생일상 앞에서 가족이 노래를 불러 줬어요.
examples.en: My family sang to me in front of the birthday table.
I was touched by the birthday meal my husband made himself.
Please keep this year's birthday meal simple.

explain: 생일에 차리는 음식 한 상을 말해요. 한국에서는 미역국이 생일 음식의 대표라서 생일상에 자주 올라가요. 보통 '생일상을 차리다, 생일상을 받다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the spread of food prepared for a birthday. Seaweed soup is the classic Korean birthday dish, so it often appears on the table. People usually say '생일상을 차리다' (to set it) and '생일상을 받다' (to be served one).

examples.en: I washed my face and brushed my teeth in the hotel bathroom.
I need to wash up, so please get a towel ready.

examples.ko: 세면할 때 쓰는 물이 따뜻하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the water for washing my face is warm.

examples.ko: 여행 중에는 세면하기가 불편할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Washing up can be inconvenient when you travel.
Please put on lotion after you wash your face.
I washed my face with cold water and woke up.

explain: '세면대', '세면도구'처럼 다른 말에 들어가는 경우가 있어요. 말할 때 얼굴을 씻는 일은 보통 '세수하다'라고 해요. 세면하다는 글이나 안내문에서 더 딱딱한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It appears inside other words such as '세면대' (washbasin) and '세면도구' (toiletries). In speech, washing your face is usually '세수하다'. 세면하다 sounds stiffer, like written notices.

examples.en: The mailman brings letters every morning.
I greeted the mailman.
When I was little, my dream was to be a mailman.
Mail carriers work even on rainy days.
I handed the package to the mailman.
I rode my bike around the neighborhood like a mail carrier.

explain: 편지와 소포를 배달하는 사람을 말해요. 직업을 가리키는 말로는 '집배원'도 많이 써요. 친근하게 부를 때는 '집배원 아저씨'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the person who delivers letters and parcels. '집배원' is also widely used as the job title. When addressing them in a friendly way, people say '집배원 아저씨'.

examples.ko: 밤에 복도에서 유령을 봤다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that someone saw a ghost in the hallway at night.

examples.ko: 유령 이야기를 들으면 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: When I hear ghost stories, I cannot sleep.
Her face was as white as a ghost.

examples.ko: 이 건물에는 유령이 산다는 이야기가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a story that a ghost lives in this building.
I wore a ghost costume on Halloween.

examples.ko: 서류에만 있는 유령 회사라는 기사가 났어요.
examples.en: A news story said it is a shell company that exists only on paper.

explain: '유령'과 '귀신'은 비슷하게 쓰지만, 실제로 없거나 사람이 없는 것을 비유할 때는 '유령 회사', '유령 도시'처럼 '유령'을 써요. '유령을 보다', '유령이 나오다'처럼 동사와 함께 외워 두세요.
explain_en: '유령' and '귀신' are used similarly, but for things that do not really exist or have no people, as in '유령 회사' (shell company) and '유령 도시' (ghost town), '유령' is the word. Learn it with verbs: '유령을 보다' (see a ghost) and '유령이 나오다' (a ghost appears).

examples.en: You have to wear work clothes at a construction site.
Work clothes should be sturdy and comfortable.
There is oil on my father's work clothes.
When I get to work I change into my work clothes first.
My work clothes were worn out, so I ordered new ones.
The company gave me two sets of work clothes.

explain: '교복'은 학교에서, '작업복'은 일터에서 입는 옷이에요. 옷 한 벌을 셀 때 '벌'을 써서 '작업복 한 벌'이라고 해요. 회사에서 맞춰 주는 옷은 '근무복'이나 '유니폼'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A 교복 is worn at school and a 작업복 is worn at the workplace. To count outfits you use the counter 벌, as in 작업복 한 벌. Clothes a company provides may also be called 근무복 or 유니폼.

examples.en: The lights suddenly went out and the room turned pitch dark.

examples.ko: 할머니 어릴 때는 시골에 전깃불이 없었대요.
examples.en: They say there was no electric light in the countryside when Grandma was little.

examples.ko: 잠깐 나갈 거니까 전깃불을 끄지 마세요.
examples.en: I'm only stepping out for a moment, so please don't turn off the light.

examples.ko: 전깃불 아래에서 책을 읽으면 눈이 피곤해요.
examples.en: Reading under electric light makes my eyes tired.
Electricity only came to our village last year.
Electric light is much brighter than candlelight, so it's more convenient.

explain: '불'이나 '전등'보다 전기로 켜는 불이라는 느낌이 있어서, 촛불이나 등잔불과 비교하는 옛날이야기에 잘 어울려요. '전깃불이 나가다'는 정전됐을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Compared with '불' or '전등', it carries the feeling of a light turned on by electricity, so it fits old stories that contrast it with candles or oil lamps. '전깃불이 나가다' is what you say when the power goes out.

examples.en: I log on to the site every morning.
I connected to the server, but it's slow.
You need a password to connect to the Wi-Fi.
Too many people are connecting right now.

examples.ko: 집에서 접속할 수 있는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to connect from home?
An error window popped up as soon as I connected.

explain: '접속하다'는 인터넷이나 서버에 연결해서 들어갈 때 써요. 사이트에 들어가는 일은 '접속하다', 로그인은 계정으로 들어가는 일이라 달라요. 'IP에 접속하다'처럼 연결하는 대상 뒤에 '에'가 와요.
explain_en: 접속하다 is used when you connect to and enter the internet or a server. Going into a site is 접속하다, while logging in means entering with an account, so the two differ. The target takes 에, as in 'IP에 접속하다'.

dis.h: log in or access a network or site

p.n: 연결하다 means to hook the line up; 접속하다 means to get on it.

examples.en: I do exercises in the park every morning.
Yesterday I got up and did light exercises.
If you do warm-up exercises before working out, your body loosens up.
The children doing exercises are cute.
My grandmother turns on the radio and does exercises.
Tomorrow I will get up early and do exercises.

explain: '체조'는 올림픽 종목이기도 하고 가볍게 몸을 푸는 맨손 운동이기도 해요. 종목을 하는 사람은 '체조 선수'라고 불러요.
explain_en: '체조' is both an Olympic sport and a light bodyweight exercise to loosen up. A person who competes in the sport is called a '체조 선수'.

examples.en: The teacher opens the roll book and calls out names.
My name is not in the attendance book.
Please stamp the attendance book.
I took the roll book to the staff room.
Looking at the roll book, I have three absences.

examples.ko: 출석부 때문에 지각 기록이 그대로 남았어요.
examples.en: The attendance book kept my record of being late.

explain: 선생님이 이름을 부르며 확인하는 걸 '출석을 부르다'라고 해요. 확인하는 일 자체는 '출석 체크'라고도 해요.
explain_en: When a teacher calls names to check, it is called '출석을 부르다'. The act itself is also called '출석 체크'.

examples.en: Click the blue button.
I clicked the link by mistake.
If you click the photo twice, it gets bigger.

examples.ko: 여기를 클릭하라고 했는데 아무 일도 안 일어나요.
examples.en: They said to click here, but nothing happens.
It makes a sound every time I click.
The menu I clicked disappeared.

explain: 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 외래어 동사예요. 휴대폰 화면에서는 '누르다'나 '터치하다'도 써요. '클릭'은 명사로도 써서 '클릭 한 번'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A loanword verb used on computers. On a phone screen you can also say '누르다' or '터치하다'. The noun '클릭' works too, as in '클릭 한 번'.

examples.ko: 후반전에 우리 팀이 한 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team scored one goal in the second half.
The second half starts in ten minutes.
When the second half came, the players were very tired.
I started watching yesterday's match from the second half.

examples.ko: 전반전에는 지고 있었지만 후반전을 잘 뛰었어요.
examples.en: We were losing in the first half, but we ran well in the second.

examples.ko: 후반전의 마지막 오 분이 가장 떨렸어요.
examples.en: The last five minutes of the second half were the most nerve-racking.

explain: 반대는 '전반전'이에요. 축구처럼 경기를 반으로 나누는 운동에 써요. 야구는 '회', 농구는 보통 '쿼터'로 나눠요. 후반전에도 승부가 안 나면 '연장전'을 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '전반전'. It is used for sports like soccer that split a match into two halves. Baseball is divided into '회' and basketball usually into '쿼터'. If there is still no winner after the second half, they play '연장전'.
